title: Refit a kettle's limescale filter: lower it into the slot behind the spout, curve out, past the rim; put the lid back
instruction: Put the limescale filter back in the kettle and put the lid back on.
context: Electric kettles' spout filters come out for rinsing and descaling. KitchenAid's instruction for putting one back: "Open the Lid. Slide the filter down into the slot behind the spout, ensuring that the curve facing outward on the filter matches the curve of the electric kettle." The hand is wider than the lid opening, so the filter is held by its grip tab and lowered from above the rim until its edges meet the slot's guides, 1 cm below the rim, with 1 mm of play; turned round, it does not fit.
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the bench top. A KitchenAid 1.25 L electric kettle (KEK1222; KitchenAid: 26.2 x 17.8 x 22.6 cm, 1.14 kg, removable lid, removable limescale filter), empty and off its power base, stands with its axis at (218, 50), spout toward +x (away from the robot), handle toward the robot. Its body is modelled as a 170 mm cylinder with a 3 mm stainless wall, its rim 230 mm up, and a 104 mm lid opening pushed 34 mm toward the spout. Behind the spout, the filter's slot: the filter rests against the wall's inside between two guide lips (1 mm radial play, 2.5 mm overlap on its edges) and two side walls (0.8 mm play a side), flared open by 1 mm over their top 3 mm, over a stop ledge 60 mm below the rim. The lid is on the kettle: an aluminium disc 112 mm across and 6 mm thick, 90 g, with a 92 mm locating plug 6 mm deep under it in the opening, its spout-side part (beyond 20 mm from its centre) raised 16 mm, and a black knob 24 mm across and 26 mm tall on top (262 mm above the bench). The kettle's power base (black plastic puck 160 mm across, 22 mm tall, 350 g) lies on the bench at (340, -240). The filter (curved polypropylene mesh plate, 34 mm chord, 50 mm tall, 1.5 mm thick, bent to the wall's 82 mm inner radius, 4 g, with a 20 mm grip tab on its inner face) lies flat on the bench with its bottom edge at (190, 220), outer (convex) face down, grip tab up, its top toward +x. Slot, filter, opening, lid, knob and base figures are estimates from product photos. Frictions: kettle and base on bench 0.6, filter 0.35, lid 0.5. The bench is the station's flat wooden table top. Both arms start at their ready pose, grippers open. Nothing else is on the bench.
scoring: Judged from the state at each moment, and only while both hands' tool points are at least 4 cm from the filter and from the lid, and the filter and lid are still (under 1 cm/s); otherwise 0. The filter is seated when it is in its slot, curve outward, on its stop within 1.5 mm and within 6 degrees of its seated orientation. The lid is on when its centre is within 6 mm of the opening's centre, it rests on the top (within 2 mm) and is level within 5 degrees. 1.0: filter seated and lid on. 0.5: filter seated, lid not on. 0.25: filter in its slot, curve outward (within 15 degrees), its bottom edge at least 5 mm down the guides, but not on its stop (lid on or not). 0 otherwise, and 0 if the kettle ever tipped past 20 degrees. Real trial: once the hands are away, check the lid sits flat in the opening, then lift it and look down through the opening: seated if the filter's top edge is level with the guides' top and its curve follows the wall. The run ends with success once 1.0 has held for 1 s.
run_limit: 1,600 steps (80 s at 20 Hz), about 2.5 times the 636-step demo
reset_notes: Nothing is random. Lift the lid off, lift the filter out by its top and lay it back on its mark, outer face down, and put the lid back on; the power base stays at its mark. About 30 seconds (estimate); nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid bodies (PhysX convex hulls; the filter with speculative continuous collision). Kettle height, width, depth and mass as KitchenAid publishes; its dome body is a 170 mm cylinder. Slot, filter, grip tab, lid opening, lid (its plug, raised front and knob), power base and frictions are estimates from product photos; the filter's mesh is a solid curved plate; the base's cord is not modelled. The kettle is empty. The demo reads object poses; a policy sees only the cameras.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (1,600 steps); demo: 1.0 (636 steps; a repeat identical). Lid set down on the bench instead of back on: 0.5; filter let go 25 mm over the slot: 0.0; not corrected by the filter's measured pose: 0.0; never let go: 0.0.
